appellations.name: Chianti Rùfina
appellations.created: Zone named in the 1932 decree; part of the Chianti DOC 1967, DOCG 1984
appellations.grapes: Sangiovese at least 60% (since the 2026 rules; 70% before), with Canaiolo, Colorino and other reds, Cabernet up to 15%, white grapes up to 10%
appellations.summary:
Rufina is the smallest of the historic Chianti subzones and, for most critics, the finest: the lower Sieve valley north-east of Florence, in the communes of Rufina, Pontassieve, Pelago, Londa and Dicomano, with only around 750 ha of registered vineyard. Vines climb from about 200 m to 500 m and more on slopes facing the Apennines; cold air from the Falterona and the Consuma pass, and a late harvest, give Sangiovese of high acidity, fine tannin and a long life. Riservas from good vintages can last for decades.

History runs deep here. Cosimo III de' Medici's edict of 24 September 1716, often called the first legal delimitation of wine zones, named four areas: Chianti, Carmignano, Val d'Arno di Sopra and Pomino, the high plateau above Rufina that is now its own DOC, an enclave within the Rufina area dominated by the Frescobaldi family's Castello di Pomino. The 1932 ministerial decree then drew Rufina as one of the seven Chianti zones.

The rules are the strictest in Chianti after Classico: new vineyards must have at least 4,500 vines per hectare, yields stop at 9.5 t/ha, wines may not be released before 1 September after the harvest, and Riserva must spend at least six months in wood. The producers' consorzio has also created TerraElectae, a private mark for single-vineyard Riservas of 100% Sangiovese aged at least 30 months (18 in barrel, 6 in bottle).

Selvapiana (whose Bucerchiale, first bottled as a single vineyard in 1979, is the subzone's benchmark), Frescobaldi's Castello di Nipozzano (Montesodi), Colognole, I Veroni, Grati (Villa di Vetrice), Lavacchio, Frascole, Castello del Trebbio and Travignoli lead.
appellations.terroir: Lower Sieve valley at roughly 200 to 550 m; galestro (flaky schistous clay) and alberese (marly limestone) with sandstone; cool Apennine air and wide day-night swings; harvests often in October.
appellations.nerd_note: Pomino, carved out as a separate DOC, lies inside the Rufina hills yet was the zone Cosimo III named in 1716; Rufina itself owes its legal identity to the 1932 decree.
appellations.classification: Subzone of Chianti DOCG. The subzone name may follow 'Chianti' only for wine grown, made and aged inside it. Subzone yields are 9 to 9.5 t/ha (8 t/ha for vineyards under 4,000 vines/ha), against 11 t/ha for plain Chianti, with a higher minimum alcohol (12% at release, against 11.5%). Riserva needs two years of ageing from 1 January after the harvest. The disciplinare treats Chianti Superiore and the subzone names as parallel categories, each with its own yields and release date. Rufina adds a minimum of 4,500 vines/ha for new plantings, release from 1 September after the harvest, and at least six months in wood for Riserva.

appellations.name: Chianti Colli Senesi
appellations.created: Zone named in the 1932 decree; part of the Chianti DOC 1967, DOCG 1984
appellations.grapes: Sangiovese at least 75%, Cabernet Sauvignon and Franc together at most 10%, white grapes at most 10%
appellations.summary:
Colli Senesi is the largest Chianti subzone and the most varied: the hills of the province of Siena outside Chianti Classico, from San Gimignano and Colle di Val d'Elsa in the north-west, around Siena itself and its Crete, to Montalcino, Montepulciano, Pienza and Chiusi in the south. That geography makes it a hidden back door to two of Italy's great reds: Brunello and Vino Nobile producers use Chianti Colli Senesi for young vines or declassified lots, and San Gimignano's Vernaccia makers bottle it as their red.

It is also the subzone with the most Sangiovese. While the 2026 rules lowered the Chianti minimum to 60%, Colli Senesi keeps at least 75% Sangiovese, with Cabernet Sauvignon and Franc together capped at 10% (15% elsewhere) and white grapes at 10%. Yields are 9 t/ha, the Riserva needs 12.5% potential alcohol, the highest of the subzones, and Riserva must spend at least eight months in wood and four in bottle. Wine may be released from 1 March after the harvest.

The style tracks the place: firm and floral on San Gimignano's sands and the Val d'Elsa, rounder and warmer in the south around Montalcino and Montepulciano. Fattoria del Cerro and Il Palagione are among the producers, and Montenidoli's Il Garrulo is a well-known San Gimignano example.
appellations.terroir: Very diverse: Pliocene marine sands and clays (San Gimignano, Montepulciano), the grey clays of the Crete Senesi, galestro and alberese on higher ground; altitudes from about 150 to 500 m; warmer and drier in the south.
appellations.nerd_note: The subzone's Riserva needs 8 months in wood plus 4 in bottle, the most detailed ageing rule of any Chianti subzone.
appellations.classification: Subzone of Chianti DOCG. The subzone name may follow 'Chianti' only for wine grown, made and aged inside it. Subzone yields are 9 to 9.5 t/ha (8 t/ha for vineyards under 4,000 vines/ha), against 11 t/ha for plain Chianti, with a higher minimum alcohol (12% at release, against 11.5%). Riserva needs two years of ageing from 1 January after the harvest. The disciplinare treats Chianti Superiore and the subzone names as parallel categories, each with its own yields and release date. Colli Senesi keeps a 75% Sangiovese minimum and requires eight months in wood plus four in bottle for Riserva.

appellations.name: Chianti Colli Fiorentini
appellations.created: Zone named in the 1932 decree; part of the Chianti DOC 1967, DOCG 1984
appellations.grapes: Sangiovese at least 60% (since the 2026 rules; 70% before), with Canaiolo, Colorino and other reds, Cabernet up to 15%, white grapes up to 10%
appellations.summary:
Colli Fiorentini is the ring of hills around Florence outside Chianti Classico: both banks of the Arno upstream and downstream of the city, the lower Pesa and Greve valleys as they come down from the Classico zone, and the slopes toward the Valdarno, in communes such as Bagno a Ripoli, Fiesole, Impruneta, Scandicci, Lastra a Signa, Montelupo, Rignano, Figline e Incisa and Reggello. These are the villa landscapes that fed Florence for centuries, and many estates belong to old Florentine families.

The rules sit between plain Chianti and Rufina: 9 t/ha, at least six months in wood for Riserva, and a delayed release date (1 September after the harvest in the rules in force to 2025; Italian Wine Central's summary of the 2026 code gives 1 June). The wines are medium-bodied and aromatic, with the cherry-and-violet fragrance of Sangiovese on mixed galestro, alberese and Pliocene sands, often softened with Canaiolo and Colorino.

Castello di Poppiano (the Guicciardini family), Fattoria Le Sorgenti, Torre a Cona and Malenchini are among the producers.

The same clays have long had another use: Impruneta, inside the subzone, has fired terracotta since the Renaissance, and its bricks and tiles went into Brunelleschi's dome. The subzone name can also appear on Vin Santo del Chianti, the sweet wine from dried Trebbiano and Malvasia that Florentine estates still make in their attics.
appellations.terroir: Arno, Pesa and Greve valley hills around Florence, about 100 to 450 m; galestro and alberese near the Classico border, Pliocene sands and clays lower down.
appellations.nerd_note: Montespertoli was part of Colli Fiorentini until 1997, when it became its own subzone.
appellations.classification: Subzone of Chianti DOCG. The subzone name may follow 'Chianti' only for wine grown, made and aged inside it. Subzone yields are 9 to 9.5 t/ha (8 t/ha for vineyards under 4,000 vines/ha), against 11 t/ha for plain Chianti, with a higher minimum alcohol (12% at release, against 11.5%). Riserva needs two years of ageing from 1 January after the harvest. The disciplinare treats Chianti Superiore and the subzone names as parallel categories, each with its own yields and release date. Colli Fiorentini requires at least six months in wood for Riserva and has a later release date than plain Chianti.

appellations.name: Chianti Montespertoli
appellations.grapes: Sangiovese at least 60% (since the 2026 rules; 70% before), with Canaiolo, Colorino and other reds, Cabernet up to 15%, white grapes up to 10%
appellations.summary:
The only subzone created after 1932 until Terre di Vinci: Montespertoli was carved out of Colli Fiorentini by a decree of 8 September 1997. It covers the commune of Montespertoli, south-west of Florence between the Pesa and Elsa valleys.

The soils are Pliocene marine sands and clays full of shell fossils, on rolling hills of about 100 to 350 m, which give a softer, more fragrant and earlier-drinking Sangiovese than the galestro of Rufina or Classico. Yields stop at 9.5 t/ha and the wine may be released from 1 June after the harvest, a few months later than plain Chianti.

Fattoria Castello Sonnino is the best-known estate to bottle Chianti Montespertoli; Frescobaldi's Tenuta di Castiglioni, the family's oldest estate, is also in the commune.

The landscape is one of castles and villas among vines and olives. The Acciaiuoli family's Castello di Montegufoni, bought in 1909 by Sir George Sitwell and long the summer home of his literary children Osbert, Edith and Sacheverell, stands in the commune. As elsewhere in Chianti, Riserva needs two years of ageing, and the subzone name may also be used for Vin Santo del Chianti.
appellations.terroir: Rolling Pliocene hills of marine sands and clays with fossils, about 100 to 350 m, between the Pesa and Elsa valleys.
appellations.nerd_note: Montespertoli's release date, 1 June, sits neatly between plain Chianti's (1 March) and Rufina's (1 September).
appellations.classification: Subzone of Chianti DOCG. The subzone name may follow 'Chianti' only for wine grown, made and aged inside it. Subzone yields are 9 to 9.5 t/ha (8 t/ha for vineyards under 4,000 vines/ha), against 11 t/ha for plain Chianti, with a higher minimum alcohol (12% at release, against 11.5%). Riserva needs two years of ageing from 1 January after the harvest. The disciplinare treats Chianti Superiore and the subzone names as parallel categories, each with its own yields and release date. Montespertoli wine may be released from 1 June after the harvest.

appellations.name: Chianti Montalbano
appellations.created: Zone named in the 1932 decree; part of the Chianti DOC 1967, DOCG 1984
appellations.grapes: Sangiovese at least 60% (since the 2026 rules; 70% before), with Canaiolo, Colorino and other reds, Cabernet up to 15%, white grapes up to 10%
appellations.summary:
Montalbano is the long wooded ridge of Monte Albano west of Florence, between the Arno and the Pistoia plain, and the subzone wraps around Carmignano, the small DOCG that Cosimo III also protected in 1716 and whose blends of Cabernet with Sangiovese follow a tradition said to date to the Medici. Communes include Vinci, Lamporecchio, Larciano, Quarrata, Serravalle Pistoiese, Capraia e Limite and the parts of Carmignano outside its DOCG.

Lower yields than plain Chianti (9.5 t/ha) and the usual release from 1 March after the harvest; the wines are generally soft, fruity and early-drinking, from sandy and clay soils on gentle slopes, with the best from the higher ground of the ridge. Since 2026 the area around Vinci and Capraia e Limite also has its own subzone, Terre di Vinci.

Tenuta Cantagallo at Capraia e Limite is one of the reference producers.

The ridge was a Medici playground: in 1626 the grand dukes walled a vast hunting reserve, the Barco Reale, across Monte Albano (the name lives on in the Barco Reale di Carmignano DOC), and Ferdinando I's villa at Artimino, 'La Ferdinanda' with its many chimneys, overlooks the vineyards. The subzone name can also be used for Vin Santo del Chianti.
appellations.terroir: Slopes of Monte Albano, about 50 to 400 m; sandstone, clays and sands; mild, sheltered climate between the Arno and Ombrone valleys.
appellations.nerd_note: Leonardo da Vinci was born in 1452 at Anchiano on the Montalbano slopes above Vinci.
appellations.classification: Subzone of Chianti DOCG. The subzone name may follow 'Chianti' only for wine grown, made and aged inside it. appellations.name: Chianti Colline Pisane
appellations.created: Zone named in the 1932 decree; part of the Chianti DOC 1967, DOCG 1984
appellations.grapes: Sangiovese at least 60% (since the 2026 rules; 70% before), with Canaiolo, Colorino and other reds, Cabernet up to 15%, white grapes up to 10%
appellations.summary:
The westernmost Chianti, on the hills south-east of Pisa around Terricciola, Casciana Terme Lari, Crespina Lorenzana, Fauglia and Palaia, within 30 km of the Tyrrhenian Sea. Pliocene marine sands and clays, low altitudes and sea air give the softest, roundest Chianti of all, often with early-maturing fruit; yields are 9.5 t/ha and release from 1 March.

Many of the area's ambitious estates now sell under the Terre di Pisa DOC or IGT labels; Badia di Morrona at Terricciola, a former Benedictine abbey estate, is one of the historic names of these hills.

The rules are those of the lesser-known subzones: 9.5 t/ha (8 t/ha in vineyards under 4,000 vines per hectare), at least 12% alcohol at release, Riserva after two years. The hills between the Era and Fine valleys are a patchwork of grain, olives and vines rather than a monoculture, and the spa town of Casciana Terme sits at their centre. The Colline Pisane name may also be used for Vin Santo del Chianti.
appellations.terroir: Low hills of Pliocene marine sands and clays with fossils, about 50 to 250 m; warm, maritime, with sea breezes from the Tyrrhenian.
appellations.nerd_note: Terre di Pisa, a DOC created in 2011 for Sangiovese-based reds, overlaps the Colline Pisane, so the same hills now have two competing names.
appellations.classification: Subzone of Chianti DOCG. The subzone name may follow 'Chianti' only for wine grown, made and aged inside it. appellations.name: Chianti Colli Aretini
appellations.created: Zone named in the 1932 decree; part of the Chianti DOC 1967, DOCG 1984
appellations.grapes: Sangiovese at least 60% (since the 2026 rules; 70% before), with Canaiolo, Colorino and other reds, Cabernet up to 15%, white grapes up to 10%
appellations.summary:
The eastern subzone, on the hills of the upper Arno (the Valdarno di Sopra) between the eastern flank of the Chianti mountains and the Pratomagno, and around Arezzo, in communes such as Arezzo, Bucine, Civitella in Val di Chiana, Castiglion Fibocchi, Laterina Pergine, Loro Ciuffenna, Terranuova Bracciolini and Montevarchi. Cool air from the Pratomagno and the Apennines gives lively, fruity Sangiovese with good acidity; yields are 9.5 t/ha and wines are released from 1 March.

The Valdarno was one of the four zones of Cosimo III's 1716 edict, and in 2011 it regained its own name as the Val d'Arno di Sopra DOC, which many of the area's ambitious estates (Petrolo, Il Borro) now prefer to the Chianti subzone.

For Chianti Colli Aretini the rules are 9.5 t/ha, at least 12% alcohol at release and two years for Riserva; the name may also appear on Vin Santo del Chianti. The subzone's identity has suffered from that competition, but its cool sites on the Pratomagno side, with a long growing season, are well suited to the fresh, cherry-scented Sangiovese that defines good everyday Chianti.
appellations.terroir: Valdarno and Arezzo hills, about 200 to 500 m; sandstone (macigno), clays and the lake-basin sands and gravels of the upper Arno; cooler and later than the western subzones.
appellations.nerd_note: The Valdarno's lacustrine terraces, the 'balze', are cliffs of sand and clay left by a Pliocene-Pleistocene lake that once filled the upper Arno valley.

appellations.name: Chianti Terre di Vinci
appellations.created: 2026 (Chianti DOCG rules approved and published in 2026)
appellations.grapes: Sangiovese at least 60% (since the 2026 rules; 70% before), with Canaiolo, Colorino and other reds, Cabernet up to 15%, white grapes up to 10%
appellations.summary:
Chianti's newest subzone was created by the revised Chianti production code approved in 2026, the first new subzone since Montespertoli in 1997 and the result of a campaign by local producers grouped as the 'Colli di Leonardo', already well advanced in 2020. It covers the communes of Vinci, Cerreto Guidi, Fucecchio and Capraia e Limite in the lower Arno hills between Empoli and Monte Albano.

Its wines may be released from 1 September after the harvest, the same late date as Rufina and Superiore, which signals the producers' ambition for a more structured, longer-aged style. The same 2026 code lowered the Sangiovese minimum for Chianti to 60% and created Chianti Rosato.

The obvious hook is Leonardo da Vinci, born in 1452 at Anchiano above Vinci; the Medici villa at Cerreto Guidi, a hunting lodge of Cosimo I, is another landmark. Cantine Leonardo da Vinci, the cooperative founded in Vinci in 1961, and Tenuta Cantagallo at Capraia e Limite are among the producers.

The subzone runs from the olive-covered slopes below Vinci down to Cerreto Guidi and Fucecchio, on the edge of the Padule di Fucecchio, often described as Italy's largest inland marsh, which moderates the climate of the lower hills. Its creation means that the area's producers can now choose between three names for the same red: Chianti, Chianti Montalbano where it overlaps, and Chianti Terre di Vinci.
appellations.terroir: Gentle hills of the lower Arno valley and the western foot of Monte Albano, about 50 to 300 m; Pliocene sands and clays, sheltered and warm.
appellations.nerd_note: Terre di Vinci was the only one of the Chianti consorzio's two big requests to pass: the region approved the subzone in 2026 but refused a Chianti Gran Selezione.
appellations.classification: Subzone of Chianti DOCG. The subzone name may follow 'Chianti' only for wine grown, made and aged inside it. Subzone yields are 9 to 9.5 t/ha (8 t/ha for vineyards under 4,000 vines/ha), against 11 t/ha for plain Chianti, with a higher minimum alcohol (12% at release, against 11.5%). Riserva needs two years of ageing from 1 January after the harvest. The disciplinare treats Chianti Superiore and the subzone names as parallel categories, each with its own yields and release date. Terre di Vinci wine may be released from 1 September after the harvest.

appellations.name: Feudo di Mezzo
appellations.grapes: Nerello Mascalese (at least 80% in Etna Rosso and Rosato) with Nerello Cappuccio; Carricante (at least 60%, 80% for Bianco Superiore) with Catarratto for the whites
appellations.summary:
The 'middle fief' is the band of the north slope just below the SS 120 around Passopisciaro, running from the Randazzo border east to the SP 7-III, between the SP 89 below and the state road above. It is one of the names that built the reputation of modern Etna: almost every pioneer of the 2000s bought or rented old bush vines here.

Girolamo Russo farms 1.3 ha of mostly century-old alberelli inherited from his grandfather, in two parcels at 630 and 670 m near the top of the contrada; the two sit on lava from different eruptions, one of them a clay-rich soil from a 17th-century flow, and the wine is juicy and red-fruited. Tenuta delle Terre Nere bottles its Feudo di Mezzo as 'Il Quadro delle Rose', Frank Cornelissen's Munjebel FM comes from here, Calcagno makes a Feudo di Mezzo from its small family holding, and Cottanera bottles both a contrada wine and a single plot, Vigna Iannazzo. Planeta's Etna winery also sits in the contrada.

Lower and a little warmer than the contrade above the road, Feudo di Mezzo tends to give rounder, more generous Nerello Mascalese than Guardiola or Rampante, while keeping the north slope's perfume and fine tannin.
appellations.terroir: North slope, roughly 600 to 700 m, below the SS 120 (cadastral sheet 20). Old lava flows weathered into dark sandy loams with pumice and some clay; mostly south- to north-facing gentle terraces. North-slope climate: wide day-night swings and, according to the disciplinare, the slope's annual rainfall of up to about 1,200 mm on the north and north-east sides.
appellations.nerd_note: Terre Nere's 'Il Quadro delle Rose' and Russo's Feudo di Mezzo come from the same contrada but different lava: Russo has pointed out that his two parcels a few metres apart in altitude sit on soils from separate eruptions, which is exactly why contrada boundaries cannot be read as uniform terroirs.
appellations.classification: Contrada of Etna DOC: one of the 133 additional geographical units (contrade) listed in Annex 1 of the disciplinare since 2011, defined by cadastral sheets, roads, streams and lava flows. The name may follow "Etna" on the label only if all the grapes come from it. It is a place name, not a quality rank. The consorzio's 2022 map counts 142 contrade (nine new ones, plus redrawn borders) pending a change to the rules; a DOCG application voted in 2023 proposes lower yields and minimum vine ages for contrada wines.

appellations.name: Santo Spirito
appellations.grapes: Nerello Mascalese (at least 80% in Etna Rosso and Rosato) with Nerello Cappuccio; Carricante (at least 60%, 80% for Bianco Superiore) with Catarratto for the whites
appellations.summary:
Santo Spirito climbs from the SS 120 above Feudo di Mezzo toward the high north slope, bounded by the Randazzo border on the west and the Panebianco-Guardiola road on the south and east. It is one of the best-known contrade on north-slope labels.

Tenuta delle Terre Nere made Santo Spirito one of its four original crus, from terraces of old vines. Anima Etnea, bought by the Tuscan Moretti family in 2010, works 1.2 ha of 90-year-old vines on a terrace at about 650 m and 7.5 ha of new plantings at 800 m in a natural amphitheatre formed by a lava flow; its Animantico comes from the old vines, Animardente blends the parcels.

Altitude and the open bowl give slower ripening than in Feudo di Mezzo just below, and wines with more lift and grip.
appellations.terroir: North slope, about 650 to 800 m, above the SS 120 on cadastral sheets 36, 37 and 61. Sandy volcanic soils on terraces and in a lava-formed amphitheatre; cooler nights than the contrade below the road.
appellations.nerd_note: Anima Etnea's upper vineyard is planted inside a bowl left by a lava flow, so the same contrada holds both 90-year-old terraces and a modern amphitheatre 150 m higher.
appellations.classification: Contrada of Etna DOC: one of the 133 additional geographical units (contrade) listed in Annex 1 of the disciplinare since 2011, defined by cadastral sheets, roads, streams and lava flows. The name may follow "Etna" on the label only if all the grapes come from it. It is a place name, not a quality rank. The consorzio's 2022 map counts 142 contrade (nine new ones, plus redrawn borders) pending a change to the rules; a DOCG application voted in 2023 proposes lower yields and minimum vine ages for contrada wines.

appellations.name: Marchesa
appellations.grapes: Nerello Mascalese (at least 80% in Etna Rosso and Rosato) with Nerello Cappuccio; Carricante (at least 60%, 80% for Bianco Superiore) with Catarratto for the whites
appellations.summary:
Marchesa lies above the SS 120 between the Panebianco-Guardiola road and the Marchesa road, next to Guardiola and Rampante in the heart of the high north slope. The disciplinare uses it as a landmark for the DOC's upper edge: the boundary runs along the 800 m contour through the contrade Pino, Sciara Nuova and Marchesa before entering the 1911 lava flow.

So Marchesa is a top-of-the-zone contrada, where Nerello Mascalese ripens late and keeps its acidity; above it the land turns to woods and young lava.
appellations.terroir: North slope, upper band up to the DOC limit at about 800 m (cadastral sheet 61), south of the SS 120. Sandy volcanic soils; cool nights and late harvests.
appellations.nerd_note: The 1911 eruption opened a line of craters on the north flank; its lava now forms the DOC boundary just east of Marchesa.

appellations.name: Passo Chianche
appellations.grapes: Nerello Mascalese (at least 80% in Etna Rosso and Rosato) with Nerello Cappuccio; Carricante (at least 60%, 80% for Bianco Superiore) with Catarratto for the whites
appellations.summary: A high contrada at the western edge of Castiglione, between the Randazzo border and the Guardiola torrent, bounded by the Panebianco-Guardiola road to the north and the Cisterna-Collebbasso road to the south. It shares the upper north-slope conditions of its neighbour Guardiola: late ripening, cool nights and fine-grained, perfumed reds.
appellations.terroir: North slope, upper band south of the Panebianco-Guardiola road (cadastral sheet 60), roughly 750 to 900 m.

appellations.name: Guardiola
appellations.grapes: Nerello Mascalese (at least 80% in Etna Rosso and Rosato) with Nerello Cappuccio; Carricante (at least 60%, 80% for Bianco Superiore) with Catarratto for the whites
appellations.summary:
Guardiola is one of the highest and most famous contrade of the north slope, a steep run of terraces between the Guardiola torrent and the Passopisciaro-Collebbasso road, climbing to around 1,000 m. Andrea Franchetti based Passopisciaro here in 2000 (the estate's address is Contrada Guardiola) and bottled its Nerello as 'Contrada G'; his Chardonnay, Passobianco, comes from the same high ground. Tenuta delle Terre Nere also bottles a Guardiola.

Height is everything here: picking comes late, and wines from sites this high tend to be pale, lifted and taut rather than broad.
appellations.terroir: North slope, about 800 to 1,000 m, on cadastral sheet 61 south of the Panebianco-Guardiola road. Loose, sandy volcanic soils on terraces held by dry-stone lava walls; strong day-night swings and harvests that can run to late October.

Rampante ('climbing') is the contrada east of Marchesa above the SS 120, bounded by the Rampante road on the east and south. Its upper vineyards reach roughly 1,000 m, among the highest on the north slope, and many of its bush vines are very old and ungrafted.

Passopisciaro's 'Contrada R' comes from the high Rampante terraces, Pietradolce (whose north-slope vineyards run from 650 to 950 m) bottles a Contrada Rampante, and Tasca d'Almerita's Tascante estate makes one too. High, late-ripening sites like these tend to give pale, high-toned Nerello with firm acidity.

appellations.summary:
Dafara Galluzzo lies just above the SS 120 at Rovittello, between the Vitalba and Battiati roads and the Sciara-Picciolo track. Benanti, the Viagrande house that relaunched Etna in the 1990s, bottles a Contrada Dafara Galluzzo Etna Rosso from alberelli on small terraces with dry lava-stone walls, some of them old and ungrafted.

Benanti describes the soils as fine, gravelly volcanic material from the 'Ancient Mongibello' phase of the volcano, with a mildly humid north-slope climate: a site for perfumed, medium-bodied Nerello rather than power.
appellations.terroir: North slope at Rovittello, above the SS 120 (cadastral sheet 89). Fine-grained gravelly soils from ancient lavas; alberello on terraces.
appellations.nerd_note: Benanti's contrada series pairs this north-slope Dafara Galluzzo with Contrada Cavaliere on the south-west slope and Monte Serra on the south-east, a neat way to taste three sides of the mountain from one producer.

appellations.summary:
Moscamento lies below the SS 120 on the east side of Castiglione, its edges set by the lava flow of 1911, the eruption that opened a line of craters on the north flank. It is a textbook case of how much soil can change inside one contrada: Tenuta di Fessina's parcel, at about 640 m and facing north-east, has thick, iron-rich basaltic soil in the upper part and some 8 m of deep sandy clay lower down.

Fessina's Il Musmeci, its flagship Etna Rosso, comes from vines planted in 1921 and 1932 here; the estate shortened macerations to 12 to 14 days and capped fermentation temperatures for a more transparent style.
appellations.terroir: North slope, about 600 to 650 m, below the SS 120 (cadastral sheet 82). Iron-oxide-rich basalt soils above, deep sandy clay below; bordered by the 1911 flow.
appellations.nerd_note: Old-vine Moscamento survives a few metres from the 1911 lava, which buried the neighbouring land: on Etna the youngest rock and the oldest vines can share a boundary.

appellations.summary:
Zottorinotto lies on the north slope at Solicchiata, bounded by the SS 120 and the Solicchiata road, with the Malpasso road to the west. It is best known through Cottanera, the Cambria family estate, which owns a 4.5 ha historic vineyard here: ungrafted vines with an average age of about 85 years, at around 800 m on sandy lava. The estate used it as the source of the massal selection for its other plantings, and its Etna Rosso Riserva from the contrada (spelled Zottorinoto on the label), first produced in 2011, is one of the reference long-aged Nerellos of the north slope. Pietradolce also farms vines in the contrada.

Old, ungrafted alberelli on loose lava sand are exactly what made Etna's contrade famous: the vines' genetic material is as much a part of the site as the soil.
appellations.terroir: North slope at Solicchiata (cadastral sheets 42 and 43); sandy lava; Cottanera's vineyard at about 800 m.
appellations.nerd_note: The label spelling Zottorinoto (one t) differs from the disciplinare's Zottorinotto, a common Etna problem: dialect names were written down in several ways before the 2011 list fixed them.

Arcuria (often written Arcurìa) lies between the SP 7-II and the Circumetnea just east of the SP 7-III, below Passopisciaro. Graci, Alberto Graci's estate in Passopisciaro (vineyards from 600 to 1,000 m in five contrade), names its Rosso and Bianco Arcurìa after it; they are benchmarks for a restrained, low-intervention Etna. Calcagno, a small family estate in Passopisciaro, also bottles an Arcurìa.

Lower than the famous contrade above the SS 120, Arcuria ripens earlier but keeps freshness from the north-slope nights.

appellations.summary:
Barbabecchi is a high, remote contrada above Montedolce, bounded by the Collebbasso and Dagrobosco roads, and the home of some of Etna's most extreme vineyards. Frank Cornelissen's Magma, the Belgian's cult Nerello, comes from ungrafted alberelli more than a century old at about 910 m here, picked late and fermented without additions; Graci also bottles a Barbabecchi from very old vines.

At this height the growing season is short and cool, and acidity stays high even in warm vintages.
appellations.terroir: Upper north slope (cadastral sheet 77), around 900 m and above, close to the upper limit of viticulture; sandy, pumice-rich young soils on terraces.
appellations.nerd_note: Cornelissen labels Magma as Terre Siciliane IGT, so one of the most famous wines from an official Etna contrada carries neither the DOC nor the contrada name in the regulated way.

appellations.name: Calderara Sottana
appellations.grapes: Nerello Mascalese (at least 80% in Etna Rosso and Rosato) with Nerello Cappuccio; Carricante (at least 60%, 80% for Bianco Superiore) with Catarratto for the whites
appellations.summary:
Calderara Sottana ('lower Calderara') is the part of the Calderara district that lies below the SS 120, between the state road and the old railway and SP 89, running east to the Castiglione border. With Feudo di Mezzo across the boundary it is the classic mid-slope cru of the north side, roughly 500 to 700 m.

Tenuta delle Terre Nere, whose cellar is in the Calderara district, bottles Calderara Sottana as one of its original crus, plus 'Prephylloxera La Vigna di Don Peppino', from a small plot of ungrafted vines well over a century old. Girolamo Russo works a hectare at about 700 m, including 65-year-old vines and young ones propagated from them, on older pumice; Benanti also bottles a Contrada Calderara Sottana.

Lower and a little warmer than the contrade above the road, it tends to give darker, fuller Nerello Mascalese with a firm frame.
appellations.terroir: North slope, roughly 500 to 700 m, between the SS 120 above and the SP 89 and railway below. Old pumice and lava sands, weathered and slightly deeper than in the high contrade; gentle terraces.
appellations.nerd_note: 'Sottana' means lower: Calderara (above the SS 120) and Calderara Sottana (below it) are separate contrade in the disciplinare, and the state road is literally the line between them.

appellations.summary:
'New lava flow' (sciara is Sicilian for a lava field) is a thin strip at the very top of Randazzo's DOC land, between the 765 m and 800 m contours, from Calderara east to the Castiglione border. The disciplinare uses it as a landmark of the DOC's upper edge.

Andrea Franchetti's Passopisciaro bottles 'Contrada S' from Sciaranuova, and Tasca d'Almerita's Tascante makes a Contrada Sciaranuova. Because the DOC stops at 800 m here, the contrada's legal strip is narrow, but Sciaranuova vineyards continue upslope beyond the line; under the DOCG proposal voted in 2023, contrada wines would face lower yields and minimum vine ages. Randazzo, the medieval lava-stone town at the north-western end of the DOC (about 750 m), has 25 contrade between the Alcantara valley and the 800 m contour that closes the denomination on this side.
appellations.terroir: North slope, 765 to 800 m inside the DOC (vineyards continue higher). Young, coarse lava with thin soils and plenty of stones; cool and late.
appellations.nerd_note: The disciplinare spells it Sciara Nuova, producers write Sciaranuova; either way the name tells you the lava here is younger than in the contrade below.

appellations.grapes: Nerello Mascalese (at least 80% in Etna Rosso and Rosato) with Nerello Cappuccio; Carricante (at least 60%, 80% for Bianco Superiore) with Catarratto for the whites
appellations.summary:
San Lorenzo lies just south of Randazzo village, between the SS 120 and the SP 230, at about 700 to 800 m, the far western end of the classic north-slope vineyards. Its soil is unusual for Etna: calcium-rich, sub-alkaline and pebbly, with mother rock breaking the surface, which Giuseppe Russo attributes to a more explosive eruption.

Russo's San Lorenzo, first bottled in 2005 from vines planted on wide terraces some 80 years ago (his father Girolamo bought them in 1991), is his richest single-contrada wine; he also makes Piano delle Colombe from a 0.6 ha parcel that ripens earlier. Several other producers bottle San Lorenzo, and the lower, middle and upper parts of the contrada give distinctly different wines.
appellations.terroir: North slope, about 700 to 800 m on the outskirts of Randazzo. Pebbly, calcium-rich, sub-alkaline volcanic soils with outcropping rock; wide terraces.
appellations.nerd_note: Russo's 0.6 ha Piano delle Colombe has been bottled separately in only a handful of vintages: a single contrada can hold sub-plots with their own ripening calendar.

appellations.summary:
Caselle lies just north of Milo village, between the Viale della Regione, Via Fornaci and the Finaita royal track, at roughly 750 to 950 m on the east slope. It is the source of Benanti's Pietra Marina, the Etna Bianco Superiore that showed how long Carricante can age: from old alberelli, it is lean, saline and citrusy when young and turns honeyed and petrol-scented, like mature Riesling, after a decade.

Milo is the only commune where Etna Bianco Superiore (at least 80% Carricante) may be made, and Caselle is one of its most prized sites: high, facing the Ionian Sea, cool and wet. Pietradolce also sources Carricante here, at about 850 m.
appellations.terroir: East slope, about 750 to 950 m above Milo, facing the sea. Sandy volcanic soils; high rainfall (the east and north-east sides are the wettest of the mountain) and sea breezes.
appellations.nerd_note: Benanti's Pietra Marina is named after a place, but not this one: there is an official contrada called Pietra Marina in Castiglione di Sicilia, on the north slope, which has nothing to do with the wine.

The name may follow "Etna" on the label only if all the grapes come from it. It is a place name, not a quality rank. The consorzio's 2022 map counts 142 contrade (nine new ones, plus redrawn borders) pending a change to the rules; a DOCG application voted in 2023 proposes lower yields and minimum vine ages for contrada wines.

appellations.summary:
Monte Serra is an extinct cinder cone above Viagrande, on the south-east flank a few kilometres north of Catania, and Benanti's home ground: the family relaunched the Etna DOC from here in the late 1980s and 1990s. Benanti's Contrada Monte Serra Etna Rosso and its long-standing Serra della Contessa come from vines on the cone's terraced slopes of ash and lapilli.

Lower, warmer and drier than the north slope, the south-east side gives Nerello with riper fruit and softer edges, and the cone's sandy soils keep it fragrant.

appellations.summary: A contrada of Biancavilla on the south-west flank, the driest side of Etna (about 600 mm of rain a year, half the north-east's, according to the disciplinare), where vines climb highest. Biancavilla, founded by Albanian refugees in the late 15th century, lies on the south-west flank; its contrade sit in the DOC band between the 600 m and 1,000 m contours, where the disciplinare records the mountain's lowest rainfall (about 600 mm) and late ripening with wide day-night swings.
appellations.terroir: South-west slope, Biancavilla, roughly 600 to 1,000 m; dry and sunny.

The consorzio's 2022 map counts 142 contrade (nine new ones, plus redrawn borders) pending a change to the rules; a DOCG application voted in 2023 proposes lower yields and minimum vine ages for contrada wines.

appellations.name: Rapilli
appellations.grapes: Nerello Mascalese (at least 80% in Etna Rosso and Rosato) with Nerello Cappuccio; Carricante (at least 60%, 80% for Bianco Superiore) with Catarratto for the whites
appellations.summary: 'Lapilli' names the small volcanic gravel that blankets much of Etna; this Biancavilla contrada sits on such loose, coarse tephra on the dry south-west flank. Biancavilla, founded by Albanian refugees in the late 15th century, lies on the south-west flank; its contrade sit in the DOC band between the 600 m and 1,000 m contours, where the disciplinare records the mountain's lowest rainfall (about 600 mm) and late ripening with wide day-night swings.
appellations.terroir: South-west slope, Biancavilla; lapilli and ash soils.

appellations.grapes: Nerello Mascalese (at least 80% in Etna Rosso and Rosato) with Nerello Cappuccio; Carricante (at least 60%, 80% for Bianco Superiore) with Catarratto for the whites
appellations.summary:
Cavaliere is the only contrada of Santa Maria di Licodia and the north-western anchor of the whole DOC: the boundary starts at Casale Brancato at 1,000 m in Contrada Somatorie and runs past the archaeological site of Tre Cisterne, with the Licodia gully to the west. Here on the dry south-west flank vines reach about 1,000 m.

Benanti makes both a Contrada Cavaliere Etna Rosso and a Bianco from high vineyards here, and Feudo Cavaliere, the Platania family estate, farms high vineyards in the contrada. Sunny days, very cold nights and little rain give wines of fine acidity.
appellations.terroir: South-west slope, roughly 800 to 1,000 m. Dry (about 600 mm a year), with strong day-night swings; sandy, stony volcanic soils.
appellations.nerd_note: Cavaliere is a single contrada for an entire commune, while Castiglione di Sicilia has 46: the 2011 list reflected which growers asked for names, not a uniform survey of the mountain.

appellations.name: Ascianello
match: Vino Nobile di Montepulciano Pieve Ascianello
appellations.grapes: Sangiovese (Prugnolo Gentile) at least 85%, the rest only Canaiolo Nero, Ciliegiolo, Colorino or Mammolo
appellations.summary: Ascianello lies north of the town of Montepulciano and extends south from Badia. The consorzio's study describes fine sands over silty clay, with deeper soils in the lower valley near the Salarco stream, which also shapes the local microclimate. De' Ricci, the historic house with Renaissance cellars under the town, has released Pieve Ascianello from the 2022 and 2023 vintages; the 2022 has been described as concentrated and luxurious.
appellations.terroir: North of the town; fine sands over silty clay, deeper soils toward the Salarco valley floor.
appellations.classification: Pieve: one of 12 unità geografiche aggiuntive of Vino Nobile di Montepulciano DOCG, named after historic parish churches and approved in the rules published by the EU in May 2025 (valid from the 2021 vintage). A "Vino Nobile di Montepulciano Pieve" must be at least 85% Sangiovese with only native partners, from the bottler's own vines at least 15 years old inside one Pieve, at no more than 7 t/ha, aged three years (one in wood, one in bottle).

appellations.terroir: North of the town; clay and sand slopes over fluvio-lacustrine terraces with siliceous pebbles.

The first Pieve releases were dense and weighty: Podere Tiberini's dark, meaty and peppery, Poliziano's broad and slowly unfolding, with Crociani also bottling one.
appellations.terroir: North, toward the Val di Chiana; coarse and calcareous sands with cobble lenses, some tuff and clay.

The upper slopes near the town have sandy, often reddish-brown soils; lower down are sandy clays, silts and clay, opening onto a wide valley to the east. Carpineto's releases are lighter and high-toned, with bright acidity.
appellations.terroir: South, toward Chianciano; reddish sands above, sandy clays and silts below.

appellations.grapes: Sangiovese (Prugnolo Gentile) at least 85%, the rest only Canaiolo Nero, Ciliegiolo, Colorino or Mammolo
appellations.summary: One of the twelve Pievi named in the 2025 rules. The first releases (2021 and 2022) were reserved and tannic: Fattoria del Cerro, Tenuta Poggio alla Sala (black cherry and stony minerality) and Vecchia Cantina di Montepulciano, in an old-school, austere style. Like all twelve Pievi it lies within the single commune of Montepulciano, and a Pieve wine must come entirely from the bottler's own vines inside it.
appellations.nerd_note: A 2022 draft of the scheme listed an area called Argiano that is not among the final twelve names; Sant'Ilario appears in the approved list instead.

appellations.terroir: South-east, next to the town; coarse sands with pebble lenses, clayier below.

Tenuta Trerose's 2021 is floral, fresh and supple with silky tannins, a sandy-soil expression of Sangiovese.
appellations.terroir: East of the Val di Chiana; sandy clays with carbonate nodules on lake-basin hills.

appellations.name: Classico
appellations.village: Fumane, Marano di Valpolicella, Negrar di Valpolicella, San Pietro in Cariano, Sant'Ambrogio di Valpolicella
appellations.grapes: Corvina and Corvinone (45 to 95%), Rondinella (5 to 30%), other local reds
appellations.summary:
The original Valpolicella: the five communes of Fumane, Marano, Negrar, San Pietro in Cariano and Sant'Ambrogio, from the gorge of the Adige at Ceraino east to Negrar, a fan of valleys running down from the Lessini mountains to the plain. The 'Classico' mention is reserved to wine from this oldest zone, for Valpolicella and Superiore and also for Amarone and Recioto, and vinification must take place inside it (with limited exceptions).

Its valleys each have a character: Fumane's steep, cool slopes (Allegrini, Monte dei Ragni), Marano's high hills, Negrar's broad amphitheatre (Quintarelli, Bussola, Bertani's Novare estate at Arbizzano), and the gentler, warmer land of San Pietro in Cariano and Sant'Ambrogio (Speri, Tedeschi, Zýmē, Masi at Gargagnago). The marogne, dry-stone terrace walls of local limestone, hold many of the vineyards.
appellations.terroir: Limestone and marl of the Lessini foothills, with some volcanic basalt; valleys between about 150 and 500 m opening south toward the Adige plain and Lake Garda's influence.
appellations.nerd_note: Masi's Serego Alighieri estate at Gargagnago has belonged to descendants of Dante since 1353, when his son Pietro bought land in the Classico zone.
appellations.classification: Geographic mention 'Classico' of the Valpolicella DOC (and of Amarone and Recioto della Valpolicella DOCG): the five historic communes defined in the disciplinare.

appellations.name: Valpantena
appellations.grapes: Corvina and Corvinone (45 to 95%), Rondinella (5 to 30%), other local reds
appellations.summary:
The Valpantena is the valley that runs north from the city of Verona toward Grezzana, east of the Classico zone, and has the right to its own geographic mention on Valpolicella, Amarone and Recioto labels. Its wines are often described as lighter-bodied and more fragrant than the Classico's, from a valley open to cool air from the Lessini.

Bertani was founded in 1857 at Quinto di Valpantena and still bottles a Valpantena range; the Cantina di Valpantena cooperative and Tezza are other names here.
appellations.terroir: A north-south valley of limestone and marl hills reaching about 500 m on its flanks, with alluvial ground on the floor.
appellations.classification: Geographic mention 'Valpantena' of the Valpolicella DOC and of Amarone and Recioto della Valpolicella DOCG, with its own delimitation in the disciplinare.

appellations.name: Valpolicella Est
appellations.village: Illasi, Mezzane di Sotto, Tregnago, Cazzano di Tramigna, Colognola ai Colli, Lavagno, San Martino Buon Albergo, Verona and others
appellations.grapes: Corvina and Corvinone (45 to 95%), Rondinella (5 to 30%), other local reds
appellations.summary:
Not a legal subzone but the name commonly used for the large eastern extension of the Valpolicella DOC beyond the Classico and the Valpantena: the valleys of Squaranto, Mezzane, Illasi, Tramigna and Cazzano east of Verona. Wines from here carry only 'Valpolicella', 'Amarone della Valpolicella' or 'Recioto' without a geographic mention.

It is where some of the most famous Amarone is made. Romano Dal Forno, at Cellore in the Val d'Illasi, built a cult on extreme concentration from its alluvial soils; Trabucchi in Illasi, Roccolo Grassi and Corte Sant'Alda in the Val di Mezzane, Marion at Marcellise and Tenuta Sant'Antonio are other leaders. The soils are more often alluvial and calcareous on the valley floors, with steep limestone and some basalt on the flanks.
appellations.terroir: Several north-south valleys east of Verona; limestone and marl hills, alluvial fans and gravels on the valley floors, basalt in places; generally later-ripening up the valleys.
appellations.nerd_note: Dal Forno's vineyards at Cellore are outside the Classico, which shows how little the 'Classico' mention says about the price or prestige of an Amarone.
appellations.classification: Informal name for the part of the Valpolicella DOC outside the Classico and Valpantena delimitations; no geographic mention is allowed on the label.

appellations.name: Maroggia
appellations.grapes: Nebbiolo (Chiavennasca) at least 90%
appellations.summary: The smallest and westernmost of the five historic subzones, around the hamlet of Maroggia in Berbenno di Valtellina. The disciplinare draws it from the Valle Serada and the Regoledo-Monastero road down through Maroggia village and the contrade of Ere, Valdorta, Pedemonte, Gatti and Camp Fop to the Valeriana road. It is rarely seen on labels.
appellations.terroir: South-facing terraces on an alluvial fan (conoide) and the slope above it at the western end of the Valtellina Superiore zone; granite and gneiss sands.
appellations.classification: Historic sottozona of Valtellina Superiore DOCG, delimited in the disciplinare. Rules as for the DOCG (8 t/ha, 24 months of ageing with 12 in wood, 36 for Riserva, counted from 1 December), but grapes for a sottozona wine need 11.5% potential alcohol instead of 11%. Wine aged or bottled in Switzerland as "Stagafassli" may not name a sottozona.

appellations.name: Sassella
appellations.grapes: Nebbiolo (Chiavennasca) at least 90%
appellations.summary:
Sassella runs from the sanctuary of the Madonna della Sassella, a church on a rocky spur above the Stelvio road, east to the edge of Sondrio. It is the most famous and often the most refined of the subzones: terraces on steep, rocky slopes facing due south, with bare granite outcrops that soak up heat ('sasso' means rock). The wines are perfumed and finely structured, with red fruit, roses and a stony length.

ArPePe's Rocce Rosse and Stella Retica, Nino Negri's Le Tense, Rainoldi and Mamete Prevostini make some of the reference bottlings.
appellations.terroir: Steep south-facing terraces between about 300 and 600 m west of Sondrio; thin sandy soils over granite and gneiss, much of it carried up by hand.
appellations.nerd_note: The sanctuary of the Madonna della Sassella marks the western end of the subzone in the disciplinare: the boundary starts on the Stelvio road just below the church.
appellations.classification: Historic sottozona of Valtellina Superiore DOCG, delimited in the disciplinare. Rules as for the DOCG (8 t/ha, 24 months of ageing with 12 in wood, 36 for Riserva, counted from 1 December), but grapes for a sottozona wine need 11.5% potential alcohol instead of 11%. Wine aged or bottled in Switzerland as "Stagafassli" may not name a sottozona.

appellations.name: Grumello
appellations.grapes: Nebbiolo (Chiavennasca) at least 90%
appellations.summary:
Grumello lies just east of Sondrio on the slopes of Montagna in Valtellina, named after the ruined Castel Grumello, a 13th-century double castle on a rocky spur now cared for by the FAI. Deeper soils and a slightly cooler position than Sassella give wines often described as softer and rounder, with a gentle, earthy charm.

ArPePe (whose Buon Consiglio and Rocca de Piro come from here) and Rainoldi are leading names.
appellations.terroir: South-facing terraces east of Sondrio, about 300 to 600 m; sandy granite-gneiss soils, somewhat deeper than Sassella's.
appellations.classification: Historic sottozona of Valtellina Superiore DOCG, delimited in the disciplinare. Rules as for the DOCG (8 t/ha, 24 months of ageing with 12 in wood, 36 for Riserva, counted from 1 December), but grapes for a sottozona wine need 11.5% potential alcohol instead of 11%. Wine aged or bottled in Switzerland as "Stagafassli" may not name a sottozona.

appellations.name: Inferno
appellations.grapes: Nebbiolo (Chiavennasca) at least 90%
appellations.summary:
The smallest of the classic eastern subzones and the most dramatic: a steep amphitheatre of rock above Poggiridenti and Tresivio, between the Davaglione stream and the Valeriana road. The name, 'hell', is usually explained by the heat that the bare rock walls reflect in summer and by the hellish work of tending the terraces. The wines are among the most powerful and long-lived of Valtellina.

ArPePe's Fiamme Antiche, Nino Negri and Rainoldi make benchmark Inferno.
appellations.terroir: Very steep, rocky south-facing terraces, about 300 to 600 m; thin sandy soils over granite, with high reflected heat.
appellations.classification: Historic sottozona of Valtellina Superiore DOCG, delimited in the disciplinare. Rules as for the DOCG (8 t/ha, 24 months of ageing with 12 in wood, 36 for Riserva, counted from 1 December), but grapes for a sottozona wine need 11.5% potential alcohol instead of 11%. Wine aged or bottled in Switzerland as "Stagafassli" may not name a sottozona.

appellations.name: Valgella
appellations.grapes: Nebbiolo (Chiavennasca) at least 90%
appellations.summary: The largest and easternmost subzone, from the Rogna stream at Chiuro east through the slopes below Teglio to Tresenda, where the road to the Aprica pass leaves the valley. Higher and cooler on average than Sassella, Valgella gives fresh, lively, aromatic Nebbiolo. Nino Negri's winery is in the 15th-century Castello Quadrio at Chiuro, and Sandro Fay at San Giacomo di Teglio makes the reference single-vineyard Valgella (Ca' Morèi, Carterìa).
appellations.terroir: South-facing terraces from Chiuro to Tresenda, roughly 400 to 700 m; granite and gneiss sands; cooler than the central subzones.
appellations.nerd_note: Teglio, above Valgella, is traditionally said to have given the whole valley its name: Val Tellina.
appellations.classification: Historic sottozona of Valtellina Superiore DOCG, delimited in the disciplinare. appellations.name: Cartizze
appellations.grapes: Glera (at least 85%), with Verdiso, Bianchetta Trevigiana, Perera and Glera lunga
appellations.summary:
Cartizze is the grand cru of Prosecco in all but name: a single, steep amphitheatre of about 106 ha in the frazione of San Pietro di Barbozza in Valdobbiadene, between the hamlets of San Pietro di Barbozza, Santo Stefano and Saccol. The disciplinare singles it out for its gradient and its southern exposure, which make a natural sun trap above the cold-air drainage of the valley.

It is the only sottozona of the DOCG, with its own name on the label: 'Valdobbiadene Superiore di Cartizze' (or Conegliano Valdobbiadene Superiore di Cartizze). Yields are capped at 12 t/ha, picking is by hand, and the wine must be made inside the commune of Valdobbiadene. The land is split among well over a hundred owners, many with only a few rows, and is among the most expensive vineyard land in Italy.

Tradition makes Cartizze sweeter than other Prosecco Superiore, usually labelled Dry, because the ripe, aromatic fruit (apple, pear, white flowers, wisteria, rose, as the disciplinare puts it) carries the sugar. Bisol, Ruggeri, Col Vetoraz, Bortolomiol, Nino Franco, Adami, Le Colture and Villa Sandi (from its La Rivetta vineyard) bottle it; Silvano Follador's bone-dry Brut Nature version shows a different face.
appellations.terroir: About 106 ha on a south-facing amphitheatre of steep slopes and terraces at San Pietro di Barbozza, Santo Stefano and Saccol. Marine sandstone and marl, shallow and well drained; sheltered by the Pre-Alps, with strong day-night swings.
appellations.nerd_note: Cartizze is legally a sottozona with a 12 t/ha cap, lower than both the DOCG (13.5) and the Rive (13), and its wine must be vinified inside Valdobbiadene, the only Prosecco place-name with that rule.
appellations.classification: Sottozona of Conegliano Valdobbiadene Prosecco Superiore DOCG (the only one), reserved for spumante: maximum 12 t/ha, hand harvest, vinification within the commune of Valdobbiadene; labelled 'Superiore di Cartizze'.

appellations.grapes: Glera (at least 85%), with Verdiso, Bianchetta Trevigiana, Perera and Glera lunga
appellations.summary: The frazione east of Valdobbiadene town that contains most of Cartizze. Rive di San Pietro di Barbozza covers the rest of its steep, south-facing slopes, so it is the closest a Rive gets to grand-cru ground. Valdo and Rebuli (Fonso Rebuli) bottle Rive wines here, and Carpenè Malvolti has used the name too.
appellations.terroir: The western Valdobbiadene hills are the steepest and coolest part of the DOCG: east-west hogback ridges of marine sandstone, marl and conglomerate, where vines face south on grassy terraces (ciglioni) and cold air from the Pre-Alps drains down the slopes at night.
appellations.classification: Rive: one of the 43 unità geografiche aggiuntive in Annex A of the Conegliano Valdobbiadene Prosecco Superiore DOCG rules, each a commune or frazione. A Rive wine must be spumante from grapes of that single place, hand-picked, at no more than 13 t/ha (against 13.5 for the DOCG), with the vintage on the label, released from 1 March after the harvest.

appellations.grapes: Glera (at least 85%), with Verdiso, Bianchetta Trevigiana, Perera and Glera lunga
appellations.summary: A Valdobbiadene frazione on the slopes just east of Cartizze, home to several leading houses. Its steep, high hillsides share the conditions of the cru next door: cool, well drained, with fine, floral wines of tension and saline length. Valdobbiadene was the birthplace of Venantius Fortunatus, the 6th-century poet and bishop of Poitiers who, the disciplinare recalls, already described its hills as a land where the vine flourishes beneath the bare mountain.

appellations.name: Renesio
appellations.grapes: Nebbiolo (Roero rosso, at least 95%); Arneis (Roero Arneis, at least 95%)
appellations.summary: Renesio is a named locality (MGA) in the commune of Canale, the main town of the Roero, in the Borbore valley at the centre of the zone. Its boundary follows the cadastral parcels listed in Annex 2B of the Roero rules. The hill of Renesio is tied to the oldest record of Arneis: a document of 1478 from Canale mentions vines called 'Ranaysii', and the grape's name is often traced to this place. Malvirà's Roero Arneis Renesio keeps the link alive.
appellations.terroir: Sandy Pliocene hills of Canale; Roero vineyards lie roughly between 150 and 450 m.
appellations.nerd_note: Renesio is split into four MGAs: Renesio itself and Renesio Incisa, Renesio Montorone and Renesio Valbellina.

appellations.name: Castelcerino
appellations.grapes: Garganega (at least 70%), Trebbiano di Soave, up to 30% together with other white grapes
appellations.summary:
The big hill north of Soave, crowned by the hamlet of Castelcerino, is one of the most important UGAs and, in the consorzio's words, a synthesis of the whole Soave system. Toward Fittà in the east the soils are volcanic, basalt on the summits with very steep flanks; on the western side slopes of 10 to 30% carry deep, very calcareous clay loams. It is one of the rainier corners of the zone, with mild temperatures, so the wines are fresh and finely drawn rather than broad.

Filippi, the organic estate based at Castelcerino, makes single-vineyard Soave from these heights.
appellations.terroir: 891.6 ha in total, 268 ha of vines (30%); summits and slopes facing south, 110 to 380 m, the highest of the Classico. Basalt to the east, calcareous clay loam to the west.
appellations.nerd_note: Castelcerino reaches 380 m, the top of the Classico, and its low vine cover (30%) shows how much of the hill is still wood.
appellations.classification: UGA (unità geografica aggiuntiva) of Soave: one of 33 named areas in Annex A of the Soave DOC rules, approved in 2019 (usable from that vintage). The same names may be used for Soave DOC, Soave Superiore DOCG and Recioto di Soave DOCG when all the grapes come from inside the UGA. A place name, not a quality rank.

appellations.name: Fittà
appellations.grapes: Garganega (at least 70%), Trebbiano di Soave, up to 30% together with other white grapes
appellations.summary:
Fittà is the volcanic heart of the hills north-east of Soave: steep slopes with fractured basalt within the first metre, fine-textured soils with basaltic stones, neutral to slightly alkaline. Much of the area is wood and scarp, rich in biodiversity, with vineyards facing mainly south and south-west on gradients of 10 to 32%. The consorzio's 20 years of weather data make it one of the rainiest and also one of the warmest parts of Soave.

The name probably comes from land given in rent (affitto). Suavia, the estate of the Tessari sisters, is based in Fittà.
appellations.terroir: 436.8 ha in total and 131.6 ha of vines (30%) on the consorzio map (its own text gives 190 ha and 75 ha for an earlier outline); 64 to 325 m, facing south, east and west. Basalt throughout.
appellations.classification: UGA (unità geografica aggiuntiva) of Soave: one of 33 named areas in Annex A of the Soave DOC rules, approved in 2019 (usable from that vintage). The same names may be used for Soave DOC, Soave Superiore DOCG and Recioto di Soave DOCG when all the grapes come from inside the UGA. A place name, not a quality rank.

appellations.name: Tremenalto
appellations.grapes: Garganega (at least 70%), Trebbiano di Soave, up to 30% together with other white grapes
appellations.summary:
Tremenalto closes the Classico zone of Monteforte d'Alpone to the north; the name probably means 'high boundary' (termine alto), where it meets Montecchia di Crosara. Its deep, fertile volcanic soils are dark brown to dark red, calcareous and slightly alkaline, on steep slopes of 20 to 35% facing north and north-east.

Cool air coming down the upper Alpone valley keeps summer temperatures lower, so the wines are notably fresh and easy to drink, an advantage in hot vintages.
appellations.terroir: 153.1 ha in total, 84.9 ha of vines (55%); slopes facing east and north, 57 to 230 m. Volcanic, calcareous soils.
appellations.classification: UGA (unità geografica aggiuntiva) of Soave: one of 33 named areas in Annex A of the Soave DOC rules, approved in 2019 (usable from that vintage). The same names may be used for Soave DOC, Soave Superiore DOCG and Recioto di Soave DOCG when all the grapes come from inside the UGA. A place name, not a quality rank.

appellations.name: Corte del Durlo
appellations.grapes: Garganega (at least 70%), Trebbiano di Soave, up to 30% together with other white grapes
appellations.summary:
A small UGA in Monteforte d'Alpone that separates the frazioni of Brognoligo and Costalunga. The name records land of the Montanari nobles bought in the early 1800s by Domenico Durlo of Terrossa. The soils are entirely volcanic (basalts and basaltic breccias); north-east-facing slopes are close to 'heroic' viticulture, while south and south-west slopes run at a gentler 15 to 25%.

The traditional pergola on contour terraces dominates, though Guyot rows planted down the slope appear on the northern side.
appellations.terroir: 42.7 ha in total, 23.4 ha of vines (55%); summits and slopes facing south and north, 40 to 200 m.
appellations.classification: UGA (unità geografica aggiuntiva) of Soave: one of 33 named areas in Annex A of the Soave DOC rules, approved in 2019 (usable from that vintage). The same names may be used for Soave DOC, Soave Superiore DOCG and Recioto di Soave DOCG when all the grapes come from inside the UGA. A place name, not a quality rank.

appellations.name: Costalunga
appellations.grapes: Garganega (at least 70%), Trebbiano di Soave, up to 30% together with other white grapes
appellations.summary: Costalunga, a frazione of Monteforte d'Alpone, is a long tongue of hill (hence the name) that runs east into the Alpone valley. Basalt is everywhere, in the soil and in the dry-stone walls and houses; the slopes are gentle and the soils fairly deep, loamy to clay loam. It has long been a reference point for quality estates in the Classico.
appellations.terroir: 121.6 ha in total, 82.2 ha of vines (68%); facing south, south-east and north-east, 40 to 140 m.
appellations.classification: UGA (unità geografica aggiuntiva) of Soave: one of 33 named areas in Annex A of the Soave DOC rules, approved in 2019 (usable from that vintage). The same names may be used for Soave DOC, Soave Superiore DOCG and Recioto di Soave DOCG when all the grapes come from inside the UGA. A place name, not a quality rank.

appellations.name: Menini
appellations.grapes: Garganega (at least 70%), Trebbiano di Soave, up to 30% together with other white grapes
appellations.summary: A UGA of the Classico hills with two pedological souls, as the consorzio describes it: basalt and steeper ground to the east, compact limestone within a metre of the surface to the west, with clay-loam topsoil over clay. Vines occupy the northern parts; the steeper southern slopes are mostly wooded.
appellations.terroir: 66.8 ha in total, 25.1 ha of vines (38%); slopes facing south and south-east, 180 to 280 m.
appellations.classification: UGA (unità geografica aggiuntiva) of Soave: one of 33 named areas in Annex A of the Soave DOC rules, approved in 2019 (usable from that vintage). The same names may be used for Soave DOC, Soave Superiore DOCG and Recioto di Soave DOCG when all the grapes come from inside the UGA. A place name, not a quality rank.

appellations.name: Castellaro
appellations.grapes: Garganega (at least 70%), Trebbiano di Soave, up to 30% together with other white grapes
appellations.summary: Castellaro is a volcanic cone at the northern edge of the Classico, the most explicit trace of the eruptions that built these hills, with moderately fine soils full of basaltic gravel. The name may refer to a ruined castle, but more likely to a castellarium, the palisaded enclosure of an early settlement. Rainfall is above the Soave average and day-night swings are moderate.
appellations.terroir: 50.2 ha in total, 21.1 ha of vines (42%); summits and slopes facing south, east and west, 140 to 260 m. Basaltic skeleton throughout.
appellations.classification: UGA (unità geografica aggiuntiva) of Soave: one of 33 named areas in Annex A of the Soave DOC rules, approved in 2019 (usable from that vintage). The same names may be used for Soave DOC, Soave Superiore DOCG and Recioto di Soave DOCG when all the grapes come from inside the UGA. A place name, not a quality rank.

appellations.name: Brognoligo
appellations.grapes: Garganega (at least 70%), Trebbiano di Soave, up to 30% together with other white grapes
appellations.summary:
One of the most historic parts of the Classico, the frazione of Brognoligo in Monteforte d'Alpone has an ancient tradition of drying grapes (appassimento) for concentrated Recioto. The soils are purely basaltic, silty clay with crushed basalt in the first metre, but slopes range from gentle pergola ground to 45% gradients worked entirely by hand, and some vines are a century old on Rupestris du Lot rootstock.

It is among the driest UGAs (under 800 mm a year over 20 years) and sensitive to drought.
appellations.terroir: 75.5 ha in total, 52.7 ha of vines (70%); slopes facing south and south-east, 50 to 160 m.
appellations.nerd_note: Centenarian Garganega on Rupestris du Lot, one of the earliest American rootstocks used after phylloxera, survives in Brognoligo.
appellations.classification: UGA (unità geografica aggiuntiva) of Soave: one of 33 named areas in Annex A of the Soave DOC rules, approved in 2019 (usable from that vintage). The same names may be used for Soave DOC, Soave Superiore DOCG and Recioto di Soave DOCG when all the grapes come from inside the UGA. A place name, not a quality rank.

appellations.name: Costeggiola
appellations.grapes: Garganega (at least 70%), Trebbiano di Soave, up to 30% together with other white grapes
appellations.summary: Costeggiola, a frazione of Soave, is clearly limestone country: steep upper slopes with compact limestone within a metre, clay loam over clay, and rich, deeper colluvial soils at the foot. The Veronese pergola dominates, mostly on contour terraces. Over the last 20 years it has been one of the wettest areas, close to 1,000 mm a year.
appellations.terroir: 291.4 ha in total, 104.8 ha of vines (36%); summits and slopes facing south and south-west, 30 to 180 m. Calcareous.
appellations.classification: UGA (unità geografica aggiuntiva) of Soave: one of 33 named areas in Annex A of the Soave DOC rules, approved in 2019 (usable from that vintage). The same names may be used for Soave DOC, Soave Superiore DOCG and Recioto di Soave DOCG when all the grapes come from inside the UGA. A place name, not a quality rank.

appellations.name: Campagnola
appellations.grapes: Garganega (at least 70%), Trebbiano di Soave, up to 30% together with other white grapes
appellations.summary: A UGA on the Soave side of the Classico hills, mid-slope and facing south to south-west.
appellations.terroir: 61.9 ha in total, 24.8 ha of vines (40%); summits and slopes facing south and south-west, 100 to 180 m.
appellations.classification: UGA (unità geografica aggiuntiva) of Soave: one of 33 named areas in Annex A of the Soave DOC rules, approved in 2019 (usable from that vintage). The same names may be used for Soave DOC, Soave Superiore DOCG and Recioto di Soave DOCG when all the grapes come from inside the UGA. A place name, not a quality rank.

appellations.name: Sengialta
appellations.grapes: Garganega (at least 70%), Trebbiano di Soave, up to 30% together with other white grapes
appellations.summary: Sengialta is the first slope on the right as the road climbs from Soave toward Castelcerino. It is crossed by the Castelvero fault, which divides the volcanic and calcareous halves of Soave, and its name carries its identity: 'sengia' is a basalt stone. The soils are moderately deep, silty clay or clay loam, with basalt often showing at the surface.
appellations.terroir: 46.5 ha in total, 24.7 ha of vines (53%); slopes facing south and east, 50 to 160 m. Mainly volcanic.
appellations.nerd_note: The Castelvero fault running through Sengialta is the geological seam of the Classico: basalt on one side, marine limestone on the other.
appellations.classification: UGA (unità geografica aggiuntiva) of Soave: one of 33 named areas in Annex A of the Soave DOC rules, approved in 2019 (usable from that vintage). The same names may be used for Soave DOC, Soave Superiore DOCG and Recioto di Soave DOCG when all the grapes come from inside the UGA. A place name, not a quality rank.

appellations.name: Colombara
appellations.grapes: Garganega (at least 70%), Trebbiano di Soave, up to 30% together with other white grapes
appellations.summary: Colombara gathers several historic sub-areas along the south- and west-facing coast of the Soave hills, from Sengialta down to the medieval town. Almost 100 ha, nearly all vineyard: volcanic clay loams in the north and east, with slopes above 25%, and compact stratified limestone to the south around Mondello, where gradients ease to 5 to 15%.
appellations.terroir: About 96.5 ha in total; slopes facing west, 45 to 140 m. Basalt in the north, limestone in the south.
appellations.classification: UGA (unità geografica aggiuntiva) of Soave: one of 33 named areas in Annex A of the Soave DOC rules, approved in 2019 (usable from that vintage). The same names may be used for Soave DOC, Soave Superiore DOCG and Recioto di Soave DOCG when all the grapes come from inside the UGA. A place name, not a quality rank.

appellations.name: Foscarino
appellations.grapes: Garganega (at least 70%), Trebbiano di Soave, up to 30% together with other white grapes
appellations.summary:
Monte Foscarino is the most famous name in Soave Classico, three volcanic cones between Monteforte d'Alpone and Soave: Foscarinetto (282 m), Boccara (292 m) and Foscarino itself (295 m). Steep slopes, moderately deep soils with crushed basalt in the first metre, and rainfall and temperatures right on the Soave average make it, for the consorzio, the best synthesis of the denomination.

The name may come from fuscus, dark thickets, or from the places where vine poles were cut. Inama built its reputation on Foscarino, including the Vigneto du Lot from old vines grafted on Rupestris du Lot.
appellations.terroir: 187.1 ha in total, 100.6 ha of vines (54%); summits and slopes facing south, east and west, 80 to 290 m. Purely volcanic.
appellations.classification: UGA (unità geografica aggiuntiva) of Soave: one of 33 named areas in Annex A of the Soave DOC rules, approved in 2019 (usable from that vintage). The same names may be used for Soave DOC, Soave Superiore DOCG and Recioto di Soave DOCG when all the grapes come from inside the UGA. A place name, not a quality rank.

appellations.name: Carbonare
appellations.grapes: Garganega (at least 70%), Trebbiano di Soave, up to 30% together with other white grapes
appellations.summary: The name points to charcoal, or perhaps a lignite pit, or simply to the very dark soil, among the most purely volcanic in Soave. Slopes are moderate to very steep, but the soils are deep and stone-free to 60 or 70 cm, with low permeability and limited water reserves. Facing mainly east at medium altitude, well ventilated, it has below-average daytime temperatures. Suavia's Monte Carbonare made the name known.
appellations.terroir: Slopes facing east and north-east, 120 to 280 m; deep, stoneless basaltic clay.
appellations.nerd_note: The consorzio's map gives Carbonare the same area figures as Colombara, almost certainly a copying slip, so treat its hectares with caution.
appellations.classification: UGA (unità geografica aggiuntiva) of Soave: one of 33 named areas in Annex A of the Soave DOC rules, approved in 2019 (usable from that vintage). The same names may be used for Soave DOC, Soave Superiore DOCG and Recioto di Soave DOCG when all the grapes come from inside the UGA. A place name, not a quality rank.

appellations.name: Rugate
appellations.grapes: Garganega (at least 70%), Trebbiano di Soave, up to 30% together with other white grapes
appellations.summary: Perhaps the most striking amphitheatre of vines in the Classico, soft and enclosing, with exposures to the south-east and north-east. The name seems to come from the rugged, wrinkled look of its rocks. The soil is entirely volcanic, arranged on ciglioni (grassy banks) and small terraces held by dry-stone walls, clayey on the surface and siltier below; summer ventilation is good. Ca' Rugate, the Tessari family estate, takes its name from the area.
appellations.terroir: 47.3 ha in total, 29.2 ha of vines (62%); slopes facing south-east, 70 to 218 m.
appellations.classification: UGA (unità geografica aggiuntiva) of Soave: one of 33 named areas in Annex A of the Soave DOC rules, approved in 2019 (usable from that vintage). The same names may be used for Soave DOC, Soave Superiore DOCG and Recioto di Soave DOCG when all the grapes come from inside the UGA. A place name, not a quality rank.

appellations.name: Coste
appellations.grapes: Garganega (at least 70%), Trebbiano di Soave, up to 30% together with other white grapes
appellations.summary: Coste, now including the area formerly called Boschetti, is a very homogeneous, north- to north-east-facing slope and, despite that aspect, one of the most densely planted parts of the Classico. The soils are wholly volcanic, silty clay and pH-neutral, on gentle gradients, and the many groves of native trees show that vines arrived here relatively recently. The northern aspect gives particularly fresh, lively wines, and the pergola makes Coste an icon of the Soave landscape.
appellations.terroir: 88.4 ha in total, 59.0 ha of vines (67%); slopes facing north and north-east, 90 to 180 m.
appellations.classification: UGA (unità geografica aggiuntiva) of Soave: one of 33 named areas in Annex A of the Soave DOC rules, approved in 2019 (usable from that vintage). The same names may be used for Soave DOC, Soave Superiore DOCG and Recioto di Soave DOCG when all the grapes come from inside the UGA. A place name, not a quality rank.

appellations.name: Monte Grande
appellations.grapes: Garganega (at least 70%), Trebbiano di Soave, up to 30% together with other white grapes
appellations.summary: Statistically the most planted UGA of all, Monte Grande lies wholly within Monteforte d'Alpone: a hill sheltered from northern winds and frost, facing mainly south-east, with slopes gentle enough to be planted almost entirely. Its deep, rich, neutral volcanic soils hold moisture even in dry seasons. Graziano Prà's Soave Classico Monte Grande is the best-known bottling.
appellations.terroir: 64.6 ha in total, 48.2 ha of vines (75%); summits and slopes facing south and south-east, 60 to 190 m.
appellations.classification: UGA (unità geografica aggiuntiva) of Soave: one of 33 named areas in Annex A of the Soave DOC rules, approved in 2019 (usable from that vintage). The same names may be used for Soave DOC, Soave Superiore DOCG and Recioto di Soave DOCG when all the grapes come from inside the UGA. A place name, not a quality rank.

appellations.name: Pressoni
appellations.grapes: Garganega (at least 70%), Trebbiano di Soave, up to 30% together with other white grapes
appellations.summary: One of the smallest UGAs of the Classico, almost at its centre between Monteforte and Soave. Early 20th-century records show winemakers paying top prices for grapes from the 'Praisoni', and the name means 'little meadow', a sign of how finely the land was divided. The soils are deep, workable clay with very few stones, exclusively basaltic, on low slopes with mediocre drainage. Cantina del Castello bottles a Soave Classico Pressoni.
appellations.terroir: 27.2 ha in total, 12.0 ha of vines (44%); slopes facing south and south-east, 80 to 190 m.
appellations.classification: UGA (unità geografica aggiuntiva) of Soave: one of 33 named areas in Annex A of the Soave DOC rules, approved in 2019 (usable from that vintage). The same names may be used for Soave DOC, Soave Superiore DOCG and Recioto di Soave DOCG when all the grapes come from inside the UGA. A place name, not a quality rank.

appellations.name: Costalta
appellations.grapes: Garganega (at least 70%), Trebbiano di Soave, up to 30% together with other white grapes
appellations.summary: As the name ('high slope') suggests, Costalta has long been one of the most sought-after sites for its exposure and height. Its soils are deep basalt, clayey and stone-free to 60 or 70 cm, with low permeability; slopes are not steep and the land is a patchwork of small pergola plots. The consorzio notes early budbreak and a long ripening season.
appellations.terroir: 72.4 ha in total, 55.0 ha of vines (76%); slopes facing south, 40 to 150 m.
appellations.classification: UGA (unità geografica aggiuntiva) of Soave: one of 33 named areas in Annex A of the Soave DOC rules, approved in 2019 (usable from that vintage). The same names may be used for Soave DOC, Soave Superiore DOCG and Recioto di Soave DOCG when all the grapes come from inside the UGA. A place name, not a quality rank.

appellations.name: Casarsa
appellations.grapes: Garganega (at least 70%), Trebbiano di Soave, up to 30% together with other white grapes
appellations.summary: Casarsa is the third tongue of hill, after Duello and Costalunga, that runs out over the Alpone valley. Its summit shows lava flows of different periods that produced substrates of different mineral make-up; soils deepen down the slope. The shape allows one of the highest shares of vineyard in the Classico. Rainfall is among the lowest of the zone, but temperatures are mild and the day-night swing during ripening is wide.
appellations.terroir: 66.0 ha in total, 40.7 ha of vines (62%); facing south, east and north, 40 to 70 m.
appellations.classification: UGA (unità geografica aggiuntiva) of Soave: one of 33 named areas in Annex A of the Soave DOC rules, approved in 2019 (usable from that vintage). The same names may be used for Soave DOC, Soave Superiore DOCG and Recioto di Soave DOCG when all the grapes come from inside the UGA. A place name, not a quality rank.

appellations.name: Pigno
appellations.grapes: Garganega (at least 70%), Trebbiano di Soave, up to 30% together with other white grapes
appellations.summary: Pigno, entirely in the commune of Soave, is the Classico in miniature: steep, sometimes excessive slopes split into small vineyards by dry-stone walls and ciglioni, with vines covering about half the land among cherry trees, hedges and woods. Basalt dominates to the west, with some limestone outcrops to the east; the soils are silty clay or loam with almost no stones. A cypress and a wayside shrine (capitello) at the crossroads of footpaths mark its skyline.
appellations.terroir: 80.9 ha in total, 40.8 ha of vines (50%); summits and slopes facing south and south-east, 60 to 150 m.
appellations.classification: UGA (unità geografica aggiuntiva) of Soave: one of 33 named areas in Annex A of the Soave DOC rules, approved in 2019 (usable from that vintage). The same names may be used for Soave DOC, Soave Superiore DOCG and Recioto di Soave DOCG when all the grapes come from inside the UGA. A place name, not a quality rank.

appellations.name: Ponsara
